name: Hôtel Regina Louvre
whyThisLocation: Faces the Louvre directly across Place des Pyramides, with the Tuileries Garden, the Rue de Rivoli arcades, and the Palais-Royal all within a 5-10 minute walk — built for visitors who want to walk to the museum rather than plan transport around it.

name: Le Meurice
whyThisLocation: Sits directly across from the Tuileries Garden and about five minutes on foot from the Louvre, putting the Right Bank's main sightseeing corridor within walking distance in either direction.

name: Hôtel du Louvre, in The Unbound Collection by Hyatt
whyThisLocation: Occupies the block between the Louvre and the Opéra Garnier, so both are a short walk away in opposite directions — a practical single base for a first visit built around the Louvre, the Palais-Royal, and the grand boulevards.

name: Hôtel Thérèse
whyThisLocation: A five-minute walk from both the Louvre and the Jardin du Palais-Royal, with the Pyramides metro two minutes away — a more moderately priced option in the same walkable pocket as the area's palace hotels.

name: Cheval Blanc Paris
whyThisLocation: Set on the Seine directly beside the Pont Neuf, a few minutes' walk from the Louvre and the Île de la Cité — as central as the Right Bank gets, and the building itself (the restored Samaritaine department store) is part of the draw.

name: Hôtel Lutetia (Mandarin Oriental)
whyThisLocation: The only historic palace hotel on the Left Bank, in the middle of Saint-Germain-des-Prés with Le Bon Marché, the Luxembourg Gardens, and the neighborhood's cafés all within walking distance — a landmark stay without ever needing to leave the Left Bank to sightsee.

name: Hôtel Bel-Ami
whyThisLocation: A few steps from Café de Flore, Les Deux Magots, and Place Saint-Germain-des-Prés, in the middle of the Left Bank's bookshops, galleries, and restaurant streets — built for exploring the neighborhood on foot rather than as a base you commute from.

name: Relais Christine
whyThisLocation: Set back from the street around a private courtyard garden in a quiet stretch of Saint-Germain, close enough to walk to the Seine, the Latin Quarter, and the Musée d'Orsay, but insulated from the noise those areas bring — a fit for couples who want quiet without giving up walkability.

name: Shangri-La Paris
whyThisLocation: Occupies a former princely residence across the Seine from the Eiffel Tower, and most rooms and suites are positioned to look directly at it — the clearest Eiffel Tower view in this guide, in a quiet residential pocket of the 16th near the Trocadéro.

name: Pullman Paris Tour Eiffel
whyThisLocation: A five-minute walk from the base of the Eiffel Tower on the Left Bank, with the Champ de Mars and the Seine both close by — a larger, more straightforward option for visitors who want to be near the tower without booking a guaranteed view room.

name: Hôtel Duquesne Eiffel
whyThisLocation: A quiet residential street in the 7th arrondissement, with top-floor rooms close enough to get a direct view of the tower, and Les Invalides and the Champ de Mars both an easy walk — a smaller, more moderately priced alternative to the area's bigger hotels.

name: Le Pavillon de la Reine
whyThisLocation: Set back from Place des Vosges behind its own courtyard, in the middle of the Marais's café and boutique streets — a quiet, historic base for couples who want to walk to dinner rather than take a taxi.

name: Hôtel du Petit Moulin
whyThisLocation: A former bakery turned boutique hotel on a quiet street just off Rue de Bretagne, in the middle of the Marais's shopping and café district — a design-forward pick for couples who plan to spend most of their time on foot in the neighborhood.

name: Hôtel Jules & Jim
whyThisLocation: Tucked on a quiet street near the Musée des Arts et Métiers, close to the Marais's boutiques and the Centre Pompidou — a contemporary, central base for first-time visitors who want walkable access to both the Marais and the Right Bank's main sights.

name: Airelles Château de Versailles, Le Grand Contrôle
whyThisLocation: The only hotel inside the grounds of the Palace of Versailles, in a 17th-century residence built by the palace's own architect. This is a destination hotel, not a convenient Paris base — it's roughly 30-40 minutes from central Paris by train, and the reason to stay is the palace itself, not proximity to the city's other sights.

name: Molitor Hotel & Spa Paris
address: 16 Avenue de la Porte Molitor, 75016 Paris, France
whyThisLocation: Built around the restored 1929 Art Deco swimming pools that made it a Paris landmark long before it reopened as a hotel. It sits at the western edge of the city near Porte d'Auteuil, well outside walking distance of the Louvre, the Marais, or the Eiffel Tower — a pick for the pools and the building, not for sightseeing logistics.
